task: Refine momentum/snap UX from primary-source research

findings: Browser snap selection considers natural endpoint, direction, visible snap areas and escape from existing positions.
Exact snap physics belong to the user agent.
scroll-snap-stop:normal permits passing several targets in a single operation.
CSS snap gives browsers access to composited scrolling and the gesture endpoint; JavaScript need not reposition content afterward.
Mandatory snapping is appropriate here because all six full-screen targets are adjacent; widely spaced targets need different treatment.

sources.type: Apple WWDC design session and transcript
findings: Continuity, immediate control, momentum-preserving gesture endpoints and familiar scrolling behavior underpin perceived fluidity.
Position-only endpoint selection can contradict flick intent; avoid unnecessary additional motion.
sources.application: Keep OS gesture physics and browser-native endpoint choice; remove the separate near-rest spring.

findings: Scrolling input can run on the compositor without waiting on the main thread.
The snap selection strategy for a fling considers its projected displacement and allows intermediate targets to be passed.
scrollend means pending position updates and the gesture have completed.
Use it for settled UI state, not to begin another scrolling animation.
sources.compatibility: Feature-detect; older-browser timers update read-only status only.

findings: scrollsnapchange identifies the actual settled snap target.
Snap events are not universal; IntersectionObserver and scrollend provide a read-only fallback.
Blocking wheel listeners can delay scrolling; passive listeners let the browser proceed.
The revision installs no wheel or touch handlers at all. Its scroll observer is passive.
scroll-behavior governs navigation/API scrolling, not the physics of user scrolling.
Adding smooth alone would not fix the native-to-custom handoff problem.
Respect the request to reduce nonessential motion.
sources.application: Reduced-motion mode disables compulsory snapping; input remains native, with no scripted relocation.

audit.previous: Native scrolling was followed by a low-speed/input-quiet gate and a JavaScript spring. Enhanced CSS snapping was explicitly disabled.
inferred_ux_problems: A near-rest delay followed by another acceleration can feel like two separate motions.
Repeated small wheel input can be pulled back to the same full-height photo before making useful progress.
Frame-based velocity filtering and script-driven scroll positions cannot consistently mirror platform-native inertia.
The old blur handler did not stop the monitoring loop.
audit.evidence_type: Source inspection, spring equation analysis and independent agent review; no claim of measured before/after FPS.

decisions.change: Use CSS y mandatory and scroll-snap-align:start with scroll-snap-stop:normal.
decisions.why: One native scrolling engine handles dragging, fling, deceleration, final alignment and interruption.

decisions.change: Remove all scripted scrollTop updates, gesture listeners, velocity polling and timed spring handoff.
decisions.why: Avoid a second animation and input contention. JavaScript observes UI state only.

decisions.change: Keep predominant visibility observation for the counter; use native snap events when supported.
decisions.why: Reflect the visible/settled photo without controlling motion.

decisions.change: Use responsive photo srcsets and decode adjacent images outside scrolling handlers.
decisions.why: Reduce avoidable transfer/decode pressure and prepare nearby photos.
decisions.evidence: Engineering implementation choice; improvement in bandwidth/frame timing has not been benchmarked.

decisions.change: Honor reduced motion with free native scrolling.

tradeoffs: The browser selects the final target from direction, momentum and layout. It can prefer the next intended target over a strict maximum-visible calculation; this intentionally avoids fighting a flick or wheel gesture.
Snap duration and deceleration remain browser/OS controlled; there is no claim of identical feel across platforms.
The UI counter's older-browser fallback timer does not affect motion.
No new library or wheel-delta smoothing layer is introduced.

validation.automated: Six tests passed: predominant visibility, native mode without interception/polling/position writes, native snap notifications, intersection/resize fallbacks, legacy status timer, refresh and cleanup.

observations: At a 757px viewport height, a very small wheel nudge returned to the current photo under the browser's native policy.
A large wheel gesture crossed multiple photos and aligned the last photo at scrollTop 3785.
An upward wheel input moved to photo 5 at 3028; immediate opposite input returned toward photo 6.
Home settled at 0 and Page Down settled at 757, with matching 01/06 and 02/06 counters.
All six photos loaded; desktop responsive selection used 1440px candidates instead of the previous fixed 1800px request.
live_browser.performance_limit: No claim of measured FPS or latency improvement; main-thread motion loop and scroll writes removed by inspection and regression tests.

validation.physical_devices: Human iOS/Android and physical trackpad assessment remains necessary.
validation.github_readback: All seven changed/added files read back identically from main before live testing.
